<rules>
- Cite every insight you rely on as [i:INSIGHT_ID], using the id exactly as given. Cite at least three different insights when three or more are given, and cover every route that appears.
- Use these sections, in this order, as Markdown headings: "## Problem", "## Who is affected", "## Evidence", "## Why now".
- Every bullet under "Who is affected" and "Evidence" ends with a citation. Every sentence that contains a number or a date carries a citation.
- Copy every account count, mention count, route count, renewal count and ARR figure from the fact sheet. Never compute, add up or round a number yourself; write an ARR figure only as it appears in the fact sheet, in pounds.
- Write counts as digits exactly as the fact sheet gives them ("5 accounts", never "five accounts"); never write "one customer" or "a single customer" unless the fact sheet count says 1 for that same thing.
- Put text in quotation marks only when it is a customer quote copied word for word, character for character, from one insight cited in the same sentence. Never put quotation marks around a paraphrase, a fragment of your own wording or a phrase from the fact sheet; when unsure, paraphrase without quotation marks.
- Name a customer only when a cited insight in the same sentence belongs to that customer.
- Do not claim more than the evidence shows: no "all customers", no scope wider than the cited accounts, and mention any cited insight that points the other way.
- Do not recommend a solution.
</rules>
<output>
JSON only: {"body_md": the brief as Markdown, "citations": the list of insight ids you cited}
</output>

{
  "body_md": "## Problem
Customers cannot correct the purchase order number on invoices generated by Keelwater's claims-handling software. This mismatch with their internal records blocks payment cycles and creates reconciliation challenges for finance teams.

## Who is affected
- Four accounts have reported this issue [i:1e3a49d688ebbadd][i:73f973717c225729][i:99ed668a91f6c801][i:f7561e6a446002ad].
- The problem has been raised through two routes: support and sales [i:1e3a49d688ebbadd][i:73f973717c225729][i:99ed668a91f6c801][i:f7561e6a446002ad].

## Evidence
- There have been four mentions of this problem across the four accounts [i:1e3a49d688ebbadd][i:73f973717c225729][i:99ed668a91f6c801][i:f7561e6a446002ad].
- Three mentions came through the support route [i:1e3a49d688ebbadd][i:73f973717c225729][i:99ed668a91f6c801].
- One mention came through the sales route [i:f7561e6a446002ad].
- The total Annual Recurring Revenue (ARR) from these accounts is £2,442,000.0 [i:1e3a49d688ebbadd][i:73f973717c225729][i:99ed668a91f6c801][i:f7561e6a446002ad].
- Greystock Liability reported, I’m trying to get our purchase order number updated on your latest invoice — it’s currently wrong... [i:1e3a49d688ebbadd].
- Penhallow Specialty Risks reported, I’m reaching out because we need to update the purchase order reference on our most recent invoice — it’s causing reconciliation issues with our finance team. [i:73f973717c225729].
- Elderfold Home reported, I’m writing to request an update to the purchase order number on your invoice — this is causing reconciliation issues, and I need the invoice contact change reflected accurately in our records. [i:99ed668a91f6c801].
- Wexmoor Motor reported, The PO we referenced doesn’t match what’s on your billing, and it’s blocking our payment cycle. [i:f7561e6a446002ad].

## Why now
- Two of the affected accounts have renewals due within the next 90 days [i:1e3a49d688ebbadd][i:99ed668a91f6c801].
- Greystock Liability has a renewal date of 2027-01-25 [i:1e3a49d688ebbadd].
- Elderfold Home has a renewal date of 2026-12-21 [i:99ed668a91f6c801].
- The most recent report was made on 2026-10-30 [i:f7561e6a446002ad].
- The problem is actively blocking payment cycles for at least one account [i:f7561e6a446002ad].",
  "citations": ["1e3a49d688ebbadd", "73f973717c225729", "99ed668a91f6c801", "f7561e6a446002ad"]
}
